# 1 Clement Chapter 19 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 19 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_019_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 19 is a transitional hinge. It summarizes the lesson of the preceding examples (humility of the great witnesses) and pivots toward the cosmic meditation of chapter 20. The key phrases "Father and Maker of the whole world" (v.2) and "long-suffering will" (v.3) prepare the reader for the vision of an ordered, patient cosmos.

The phrase "the goal of peace which was handed down to us from the beginning" (*skopos tēs eirēnēs*) suggests that peace is not just a personal virtue but a *paradosis* — a tradition handed down through the community. This is ecclesiological: peace is part of the apostolic deposit.

---

## Chapter 19

**19:1** The humility and humble submission of so many great and attested men has made better not only us but also the generations before us, who received his oracles in fear and truth.

**19:2** Since therefore we share in so many great and glorious deeds, let us hasten toward the goal of peace which was handed down to us from the beginning, and let us look to the Father and Maker of the whole world, and hold fast to his magnificent and surpassing gifts of peace and beneficence.

**19:3** Let us behold him with the eyes of our mind; let us consider his long-suffering will; let us reflect how free from wrath he is toward all his creation.

---

*SOPHIA consensus translation. Completed 2026-03-17.*
